title: Agent purpose is undefined or expands without approval
problem: The agent has no bounded business purpose, so new prompts, tools or integrations silently broaden what it may do.
check_method: Compare the declared purpose, production prompts, tool catalogue and recent change history; flag capabilities that are not necessary for an approved use case. Review the exact assessed version against the approved governance record for “Agent purpose is undefined or expands without approval”; compare the declared purpose, permitted and prohibited outcomes, prompts, tools, integrations and recent change history, and require explicit approval for any material scope expansion.
solution: Record and approve a versioned agent purpose, permitted outcomes, prohibited outcomes, accountable owner and material scope boundaries. Require an attributable change record and accountable human approval before expanding prompts, tools, integrations, data access, network reach or execution authority.
mappings: NIST AI RMF 1.0 GOVERN/MAP|ISO/IEC 42001:2023 management system|OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 ASI10
pass_condition: ARL-KB-001 passes only when the exact assessed version has a bounded, versioned and accountable purpose; current prompts, tools, integrations and data access are necessary for that approved purpose or explicitly approved as scope changes; and version-bound evidence records the reviewer, timestamp and digest.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-001 fails when the agent has no bounded business purpose, so new prompts, tools or integrations silently broaden what it may do, when a current capability cannot be justified by the approved purpose, when a material scope expansion lacks accountable approval, or when the conclusion is unsupported by version-bound review evidence.
retest_acceptance: ARL-KB-001: The exact remediated version has an explicit, versioned and attributable purpose.|ARL-KB-001: Permitted and prohibited outcomes are documented and consistent with the assessed capabilities.|ARL-KB-001: Every material prompt, tool, integration, data-access or authority capability is necessary for the approved purpose or has an attributable approved scope-change record.|ARL-KB-001: A proposed material scope expansion cannot be treated as approved without the required accountable human decision.|ARL-KB-001: Reviewer identity, timestamp, assessed version, evidence digest, known limitations and scope decision are recorded.

title: No accountable risk owner
problem: No named person is responsible for accepting residual risk, funding remediation or stopping deployment.
check_method: Identify the exact assessed system, version, environment and scope. Inspect the current risk-owner appointment, governance record or equivalent authoritative evidence. Verify that a named accountable risk owner is assigned to the assessed system and scope, that the appointment is current, attributable and not expired, and that the documented authority includes the ability to accept residual risk, fund or authorise remediation, and stop or withhold deployment. Where delegation exists, verify its scope, authority, effective date and expiry. Record the reviewer, timestamp and evidence digest.
solution: Appoint a named accountable risk owner for the exact assessed system and scope. Document the owner's role, contact, effective date, expiry where applicable, and explicit authority for residual-risk acceptance, remediation funding or authorisation, and deployment stop or withholding. Define deputies or delegation only where their authority and scope are explicitly recorded.
mappings: NIST AI RMF 1.0 GOVERN|ISO/IEC 42001:2023 leadership
pass_condition: ARL-KB-002 passes only when the exact assessed system and scope have a named accountable risk owner with documented authority to accept residual risk, fund or authorise remediation, and stop or withhold deployment; the ownership record is current and attributable; and version-bound evidence records the reviewer, timestamp and digest.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-002 fails when no named person is responsible for accepting residual risk, funding remediation or stopping deployment, when ownership is unnamed, expired or not bound to the assessed system and scope, when any required authority is absent or unsupported, or when the conclusion lacks version-bound review evidence.
retest_acceptance: ARL-KB-002: A named accountable risk owner is recorded for the exact assessed system and scope.|ARL-KB-002: Residual-risk acceptance, remediation funding or authorisation, and deployment stop or withholding authorities are explicitly documented.|ARL-KB-002: Appointment and delegation records are current, attributable and not expired.|ARL-KB-002: Missing, expired, unnamed or incomplete ownership evidence results in hold or review rather than control satisfaction.|ARL-KB-002: Reviewer identity, assessed version, timestamp and evidence digest are recorded.

title: Prohibited uses and harm boundaries are missing
problem: The organisation has not stated which users, decisions, sectors or actions the agent must never support.
check_method: Identify the exact assessed system, version, environment and scope. Review the versioned prohibited-use and harm boundaries and determine which users, decisions, sectors, actions or outcomes are explicitly forbidden or require human escalation. Trace those boundaries to the relevant prompts, policy rules, tool restrictions or other enforcement points. Execute an authorised positive case and representative forbidden requests using safe non-production conditions. Verify that legitimate in-scope use remains available and that each prohibited case is refused or escalated before the prohibited material action occurs.
solution: Define a versioned prohibited-use and harm-boundary policy covering relevant users, decisions, sectors, actions and outcomes. Map each material boundary to an enforceable control point, define refusal and escalation behaviour, assign an accountable owner, and test representative allowed and prohibited cases.

title: Risk classification does not match real impact
problem: The agent is treated as low risk even though it can move money, alter records, affect rights, disclose sensitive data or control infrastructure.
check_method: Identify the exact assessed version and declared risk tier. Inventory the system's reachable assets, identities, data, tools, integrations, permissions, maximum action values, reversibility, affected people, scale and dependency chains. Determine the maximum credible impact supported by observed evidence, then compare that impact with the declared risk tier. Any classification decision or reclassification must be made by an accountable human reviewer and recorded with version-bound evidence.
solution: Reclassify the system using evidence of actual reachable authority, assets, data exposure, maximum action values, reversibility, scale, affected people and downstream dependency chains. Bind the resulting tier and rationale to the exact assessed version and require accountable human approval of any classification decision.
applicability: agents with tools or consequential outputs
mappings: NIST AI RMF 1.0 MAP|ISO/IEC 23894:2023 risk context|OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 ASI08
pass_condition: ARL-KB-004 passes only when the declared risk tier for the exact assessed version is supported by evidence of the system's actual authority, reachable assets, data exposure, reversibility, scale, affected people and dependency chains; the declared tier is not lower than the tier required by the maximum credible observed impact; and the human reviewer, timestamp, rationale and evidence digest are recorded.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-004 fails when the declared risk tier understates the maximum credible impact of the system's actual reachable capabilities, including the ability to move money, alter records, affect rights, disclose sensitive data, control infrastructure or cause material downstream effects; when impact-relevant capabilities are omitted from classification; or when the classification conclusion lacks accountable, version-bound human review evidence.

title: Trust boundaries and data flows are undocumented
problem: Reviewers cannot see where untrusted input becomes model context, where identities change, or where outputs reach tools and external systems.
check_method: Identify the exact assessed version, environment and scope. Build or obtain the current architecture and data-flow model, then verify it against source code, configuration, runtime wiring and documented integrations. Trace representative flows from user input through model context and orchestration to tools, stores, network destinations, human approvals and audit evidence. Confirm that every material actor, trust-zone transition, data destination, authority boundary and known alternate path is represented, and record any limitation or unresolved path.
solution: Create and maintain a versioned architecture model for the exact assessed system. Document material actors, trust zones, data flows, models, memory, tools, stores, network destinations, authority boundaries, approval points and evidence paths. Bind the model to implementation evidence and update it whenever material architecture or scope changes.
mappings: NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 secure design|NIST AI RMF 1.0 MAP
pass_condition: ARL-KB-005 passes only when the exact assessed version has a current architecture model that identifies all material actors, trust zones, data flows, stores, tools, network destinations, authority boundaries, human approval points and evidence paths; representative documented flows are supported by observed source or configuration evidence; known limitations and alternate paths are recorded; and the review is version-bound and attributable.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-005 fails or requires review when a material actor, trust boundary, data flow, tool, store, network destination, approval point or alternate path is missing, stale, contradicted by observed implementation, or unsupported by version-bound evidence.

title: Data classification is absent or inconsistent
problem: Prompts, memories, logs and tool arguments may contain personal, confidential, regulated or secret data without suitable handling rules.
check_method: Identify the exact assessed version, environment and scope. Review the current data classification and handling policy, supported classes and restricted classes. Trace representative data through model context, memory, tool arguments, tool results, runtime logging, persistence and export paths. Verify that classification is applied consistently, that restricted classes receive the documented redaction, denial, retention or export treatment, and that classification or handling failure does not silently downgrade protection.
solution: Define and maintain a versioned data-classification and handling policy. Classify data before or at entry to material processing paths, propagate or recompute classification where needed, and enforce class-appropriate redaction, denial, retention and export rules at each relevant destination.
mappings: ICO AI and Data Protection security and minimisation|NIST AI 600-1 data privacy
pass_condition: ARL-KB-006 passes only when relevant data is consistently classified for the exact assessed version, restricted classes receive the documented handling across applicable model, tool, log, persistence, retention and export paths, classification or handling failure does not silently reduce protection, and the conclusion is supported by version-bound attributable evidence.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-006 fails or requires review when relevant data is unclassified, inconsistently classified, downgraded between components, sent to a destination incompatible with its class, retained or exported contrary to policy, or when required handling evidence is absent.
retest_acceptance: ARL-KB-006: The exact remediated version has a documented and versioned classification and handling policy.|ARL-KB-006: Representative data receives the expected classification across applicable processing paths.|ARL-KB-006: Restricted data receives the documented redaction, denial, retention and export treatment.|ARL-KB-006: Classification or handling failure does not silently downgrade protection.|ARL-KB-006: Reviewer identity, timestamp, exact assessed version, policy version and evidence digest are recorded.

title: Third-party AI and tool providers are not assessed
problem: A model, MCP server, plugin, vector service or observability vendor can change behaviour, process data elsewhere or become compromised.
check_method: Inventory every external provider or remotely operated dependency that can influence agent behaviour, receive data, provide model output, expose tools or affect deployment. Compare the observed provider set and configuration with the approved system scope. For each applicable provider, review the approved purpose, data sent or received, deployment or endpoint configuration, version/change controls, incident or compromise response, disablement or fallback path, and evidence of accountable approval. Treat dormant but activatable external-provider paths as review items when they can be enabled without an approved scope change. Use synthetic/local evidence only and do not exercise real third-party services without explicit authorisation.
solution: Maintain an approved provider register tied to system scope and exact configuration; document data and network boundaries; require accountable approval for provider or endpoint changes; define incident, disablement, fallback and exit controls; and reassess after material provider changes.
mappings: NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 supply-chain security|OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 ASI04
pass_condition: ARL-KB-007 passes only when every applicable external provider or remotely operated dependency observed in the exact assessed version is identified and consistent with the approved scope; its relevant data, network and authority boundaries are documented; material provider or configuration changes require accountable review; and version-bound evidence supports the conclusion. A dormant external-provider path does not pass merely because credentials are currently absent if it can be activated outside the approved change process.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-007 fails when an external AI, MCP, plugin, vector, observability or other provider can influence behaviour, receive data or become active without being identified and approved; when observed provider/configuration state differs materially from the approved scope without accountable review; when provider change, compromise, fallback or disablement is unmanaged; or when the conclusion is unsupported by version-bound evidence.
retest_acceptance: ARL-KB-007: Every applicable external provider or remotely operated dependency observed in the exact remediated version is identified and reconciled with the approved scope.|ARL-KB-007: Relevant provider purpose, configuration, data, network and authority boundaries are documented.|ARL-KB-007: Dormant or alternate external-provider paths are explicitly recorded with their activation and approval status.|ARL-KB-007: Material provider or configuration changes require accountable review before they inherit prior approval.|ARL-KB-007: Reviewer identity, timestamp, exact assessed version, provider configuration and evidence digest are recorded.

title: Legal basis, transparency or user notice is unsupported
problem: The organisation cannot show why personal data is processed, what the agent does, or how affected people can exercise rights.
check_method: Identify the personal data and human interactions present in the exact assessed version. Compare the observed processing, purposes, recipients, model or tool destinations, retention and user journey with the organisation's documented privacy analysis and notices. Verify that the organisation records the purpose and asserted legal basis for applicable processing, provides appropriate transparency about the agent and material data use, defines retention and rights-handling routes, and assigns accountable ownership. ARL verifies the presence, traceability and consistency of this evidence; it does not determine legal sufficiency or provide legal advice. Use synthetic or non-production data and do not exercise rights against real people or third parties during the test.
solution: Document the applicable processing purpose and organisation-approved legal-basis analysis; align notices with observed agent and data behaviour; document relevant retention and rights-handling routes; assign accountable privacy ownership; and review the records after material changes to data, purpose, provider or user journey.

title: Security-relevant changes bypass review
problem: Prompt, model, tool, policy or data-source changes can reach production without threat modelling, tests or approval.
check_method: Inspect version history, change records, review evidence and deployment provenance for security-relevant changes to prompts, models, tools, permissions, policies, schemas, data sources, dependencies and providers. For a representative material change, trace the exact source version through classification, security review, required tests, accountable approval and deployment. Verify that approval and test evidence are bound to the exact version or immutable artefact that reaches production, and that a changed, unreviewed or stale version cannot inherit approval from an earlier version. Confirm that material architecture or scope changes trigger reassessment or revalidation and that rollback preserves a known reviewed state.
solution: Classify security-relevant changes; require appropriate review and negative tests; bind approvals and evidence to immutable versions or artefact digests; enforce reviewed deployment provenance; trigger reassessment after material scope or architecture changes; and maintain a known-good rollback version.
mappings: NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 secure development/deployment|NIST AI RMF 1.0 MANAGE
pass_condition: ARL-KB-009 passes only when security-relevant production changes are identified before deployment, receive the required review and tests, and have accountable approval bound to the exact deployed version or immutable artefact; stale evidence or approval from a different material version cannot authorize the change; material scope or architecture changes trigger reassessment or revalidation; and attributable deployment evidence supports the conclusion.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-009 fails when a security-relevant prompt, model, tool, permission, policy, schema, data-source, dependency or provider change can become authoritative in production without the required review, tests or approval; when approval or evidence can be reused across a materially different version; when production provenance cannot identify the reviewed artefact; or when a material scope or architecture change does not trigger required reassessment or revalidation.

title: Acceptance criteria are vague or based on a score alone
problem: A high aggregate score can hide a critical unresolved action, missing approval, tenant breach or untested recovery path.
check_method: Identify the exact assessed version and the decision being made. Inspect the documented acceptance criteria, readiness or deployment gates, evidence requirements, unresolved-risk rules, approval authority, recovery or rollback requirements and known limitations. Verify that mandatory blockers are evaluated independently of any aggregate score and that critical unresolved findings, missing required evidence, failed exact retests, missing accountable approval or required recovery evidence cannot be averaged away. Trace a representative decision to the exact evidence and named human authority that accepted, rejected or held the system.
solution: Define explicit pass, hold and fail criteria for critical findings, required approvals, exact retests, recovery or rollback readiness, evidence quality and known limitations. Treat mandatory blockers independently from aggregate scores, assign a named human decision authority, and preserve the exact evidence supporting every readiness or deployment decision.
mappings: NIST AI RMF 1.0 MEASURE/MANAGE|ISO/IEC 23894:2023 risk treatment
pass_condition: ARL-KB-010 passes only when the assessed readiness or deployment decision is governed by explicit mandatory gates; required evidence, approvals, exact retests and recovery requirements are attributable to the assessed version; an unresolved mandatory blocker cannot be hidden or offset by a high aggregate score; known limitations and residual risks remain visible; and the final decision is made by the documented human authority.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-010 fails or requires review when acceptance criteria are undefined, ambiguous or score-only; when a high aggregate score can override or obscure an unresolved mandatory blocker; when required approval, exact retest, recovery, rollback or other decision evidence is missing; when known limitations or residual risks are not visible to the decision-maker; or when the readiness decision is unsupported by attributable version-bound evidence.

title: AI assets and agents are not fully inventoried
problem: Unknown agents, models, prompts, tools or data stores escape assessment, patching and ownership.
check_method: Enumerate observable repositories, deployments, agents, model endpoints, prompt configurations, MCP servers, tools, data stores, service identities and scheduled jobs; reconcile them with the authoritative declared inventory. Verify each required inventory record has an accountable owner, purpose, environment, version or identifier, relevant data or permission scope, dependencies and lifecycle status. Record undeclared observed assets, stale declared assets and unresolved ownership or version gaps.
solution: Maintain a continuously reconciled inventory with owner, purpose, environment, version, data class, permissions, dependencies and lifecycle status.
mappings: NIST AI RMF 1.0 GOVERN/MAP|NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 asset management
pass_condition: ARL-KB-011 passes only when every in-scope asset observed through the documented discovery sources is represented in the current authoritative inventory, required ownership and lifecycle metadata is present, no unresolved undeclared or stale asset remains, and the reconciliation evidence is attributable, reproducible and bound to the assessed version.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-011 fails when an in-scope observed AI asset or agentic component is absent from the authoritative inventory, a declared asset cannot be reconciled to the assessed system, required ownership or lifecycle information is missing, or the inventory reconciliation cannot be reproduced from version-bound evidence.

title: Shadow or experimental agents reach real data
problem: A prototype, notebook, personal API key or unofficial agent can reach production data, tools or services outside approved controls.
check_method: Reconcile approved experimental environments, identities and providers with identity, network, billing, provider and audit logs to identify undeclared agent or model usage. Inspect the controls separating experimentation from production. In an owner-authorised non-production or production-equivalent test environment, verify that a prototype, notebook or unofficial-agent identity cannot authenticate to, route to or retrieve production-equivalent data and services through prohibited paths, while the approved sandbox workflow remains usable. Bind all observations to the exact assessed version and configuration.
solution: Separate experimentation from production with distinct accounts, projects, networks and credentials; provide governed sandboxes with synthetic data; block unapproved providers and routes; prohibit personal credentials for production access; and rotate exposed shadow credentials after containment.
mappings: NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 secure deployment
pass_condition: ARL-KB-012 passes only when approved experimental workflows remain confined to their authorised sandbox scope, no tested prototype, notebook, personal credential or unofficial-agent path can reach prohibited production-equivalent data or services, attempted boundary crossings are blocked or otherwise prevented before access occurs, and attributable version-bound evidence demonstrates the result.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-012 fails when an experimental or unofficial AI component can authenticate to, route to, retrieve from or act on prohibited production data or services; when personal or unmanaged credentials provide such access; when an undocumented exception bypasses the approved environment boundary; or when the claimed separation cannot be demonstrated with reproducible version-bound evidence.
retest_acceptance: ARL-KB-012: The exact remediated version preserves the documented separation between experimental and production identities, data, tools, networks and provider accounts.|ARL-KB-012: The approved experimental workflow completes successfully using only authorised sandbox resources and synthetic or explicitly approved test data.|ARL-KB-012: A dedicated simulated shadow or experimental identity cannot reach the documented prohibited production-equivalent data, credential, tool or service paths, and evidence of the boundary-crossing attempt is recorded.|ARL-KB-012: Reviewer identity, timestamp, assessed version, relevant configuration digests, known limitations and residual-risk or deployment decision are recorded.

title: External destinations and egress paths are unknown
problem: The agent can send data to domains, webhooks or tools that are absent from the threat model.
check_method: Compare declared architecture and network configuration with code, tool definitions and observed runtime DNS/HTTP activity. Enumerate domains, IP destinations, proxies, redirects, callbacks, webhooks and tool endpoints, including dynamically selected targets. In an owner-authorised non-production environment, attempt approved and unapproved destinations and verify enforcement occurs before external transmission.
solution: Maintain an explicit destination and egress inventory; enforce deny-by-default outbound policy using controlled proxy, firewall or equivalent enforcement; apply destination allowlists and DNS/IP validation; constrain dynamic destinations; and record privacy-aware runtime egress evidence.
mappings: OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 ASI02
pass_condition: ARL-KB-013 passes when the observed outbound destinations and routes match the documented authorised inventory, unapproved or unknown destinations are denied or explicitly routed to review before external transmission, and version-bound evidence shows the enforcement decision.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-013 fails when an outbound domain, IP, webhook, callback, tool endpoint or network route is reachable but absent from the assessed inventory or approved policy, or when an unapproved destination can be reached before the applicable egress control detects or blocks it.
retest_acceptance: ARL-KB-013: All observed external destinations and routes for the exact remediated version are represented in the approved inventory.|ARL-KB-013: Authorised in-scope destinations remain reachable through the documented egress path.|ARL-KB-013: Undeclared, unapproved and relevant dynamically redirected destinations are denied or held for explicit review before external transmission.|ARL-KB-013: Reviewer identity, timestamp, deployed version, evidence digest, known limitations and deployment decision are recorded.

title: Credential inventory is incomplete
problem: Long-lived API keys, tokens, cookies or private keys remain active without known owner, scope or rotation plan.
check_method: Enumerate secret stores, environment references, CI variables, service accounts and observed runtime credential use without exposing secret values. Reconcile discovered credentials against the approved inventory and identify orphaned, duplicate, unused, over-scoped or non-expiring credentials.
solution: Assign ownership and expiry, use short-lived workload identity, reduce scopes, revoke unused credentials and monitor anomalous use.
mappings: NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 secure development/operation|OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 ASI03
pass_condition: ARL-KB-014 passes when all credentials available to the assessed agent are represented in the approved inventory with attributable ownership, necessary scope and documented lifecycle controls, and no tested active credential is orphaned or unexplained.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-014 fails when an active credential available to the assessed system lacks an accountable owner, purpose, known scope, lifecycle state or required rotation/expiry control, or when runtime use cannot be reconciled to the approved inventory.

title: Memory and vector stores are untracked
problem: Persistent context, embeddings and retrieved documents may outlive the project or cross environments and tenants.
check_method: Inventory persistent memory stores, vector databases, indexes, namespaces, replicas, caches, backups and deletion paths. Map which assessed identities can read or write each store, which environment and tenant or project boundary applies, and whether retention and deletion behaviour are documented.
solution: Register stores as governed assets, isolate namespaces, restrict write paths, implement retention/deletion and test restoration without cross-tenant data.

title: Model versions and digests are not pinned
problem: The same model name can resolve to different weights or behaviour, invalidating prior tests and approvals.
check_method: Record provider, model identifier, immutable revision or digest where available, local artifact hash where applicable, system-prompt/configuration version and security-relevant inference settings. Resolve the deployed runtime to those identifiers, detect mutable aliases or drift, and verify that a material model or configuration change requires targeted reassessment before prior approval is reused.
solution: Pin immutable versions, record provenance, detect drift and require targeted retesting before accepting a changed model or configuration.
mappings: OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 LLM03|NCSC Secure AI Development 1.0 supply chain
pass_condition: ARL-KB-016 passes when the assessed model and security-relevant configuration are attributable to an exact version or immutable evidence reference and material drift cannot silently inherit prior assessment evidence.
fail_condition: ARL-KB-016 fails when the deployed model or relevant inference configuration can change without an attributable version or digest, or when evidence from a materially different model/configuration remains accepted as current.
